text: Oh no, wild Qubits have found us! Let's understand our enemy before we defend ourselves.
See that strange | ⟩ notation? That just holds the state of the qubit. If a dangerous |0⟩ slips past our defenses, we lose HP!
Our goal is to flip them into harmless |1⟩ states so we don't take damage.
Grab the X flipper from the top bar! It magically flips a |0⟩ into a |1⟩ as the enemy passes through.
Click a grid line to place your X flipper. Right-click if you want to remove it. Press ▶ when you're ready!
Perfect! A gate acts on every qubit that passes through it, so one well-placed gate can handle a whole lane.
Great job stopping those Qubits! By the way, those flippers you used? In quantum mechanics, they are actually called 'gates'.
Mathematically, the X gate swaps the |0⟩ and |1⟩ amplitudes (the α and β). This is like spinning the sphere completely upside down around the X-axis.
The Y gate spins it around the Y-axis. Mathematically, it also swaps the amplitudes, but multiplies them by the imaginary numbers -i and i!
The Z gate just spins the sphere around its equator, leaving the probabilities the same but multiplying the bottom number by -1.
Look out! We have 3 lanes now. Try putting exactly one gate (X, Y, and Z) in each lane to see how they affect the qubits! You might take a little damage, but you'll survive!
You survived! Notice how multiplying by -1 couldn't block the damage for states on the equator? We'll need a new trick for that next.
Dummy level: phases matter once a Hadamard turns them into amplitudes.
